articleTitle: Optimizing Chronic Kidney Disease Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Review of Metaheuristic Algorithms and Their Applications in Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The usage of metaheuristic algorithms for the diagnosis and classification of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is investigated in this work. To improve feature selection and classification accuracy, this study proposes several optimization algorithms including Genetic Algorithm (GA), Firefly Optimization Algorithm (FOA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). These methods are combined in the proposed method with machine learning models including support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF). With some methods reaching up to ${9 9. 5 6 \%}$ accuracy, this proposed method obtains greater performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score by means of empirical evaluation employing CKD datasets. This study indicated the efficient handling of metaheuristic approaches managing issues in healthcare applications including noisy, unbalanced, and high dimensional datasets.

articleTitle: Innovative Machine Learning Techniques for Accurate Detection of Bacterial Blight in Rice Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Bacterial blight is a devastating disease that can significantly impact rice production. Early and accurate detection of the disease is crucial for effective management. This research proposes a deep learning-based approach, specifically utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to identify and classify different severity levels of bacterial blight in rice plants. The proposed model involves a multi-step process, including data preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification. The CNN architecture is designed to capture the visual characteristics of infected plants, enabling accurate disease diagnosis. The model’s performance is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. By implementing this automated disease detection system, farmers can make timely decisions regarding disease management strategies, leading to improved crop yields and reduced economic losses. This research contributes to the advancement of precision agriculture and sustainable food production.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of ECG Compression Techniques Using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are crucial for diagnosing and monitoring heart health but can produce significant data files that create challenges for storage, transmission, and analysis in eHealth systems. This paper presents various ECG compression techniques implemented on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to mitigate these challenges. The study covers lossless methods like Run-Length Encoding (RLE) and Differential Pulse Code Modulation (DPCM) as well as lossy methods such as Wavelet Transform and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Performance metrics, including Compression Ratio (CR), Percent Root Mean Square Difference (PRD), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Power Consumption, and Latency, are analyzed to assess their effectiveness. The findings indicate that while SVD on PYNQ-Z2 FPGA achieves the highest compression ratio, methods like SPIHT and hybrid approaches provide a balanced trade-off between compression efficiency and signal fidelity. Future work is suggested to focus on optimizing power consumption, improving compression ratios, and reducing latency. This paper provides insights into developing efficient, real-time ECG compression solutions suitable for resource-constrained eHealth applications.

articleTitle: Wearable Health Monitoring Devices and Technology’s Impact on Work-Life Balance for Women Seafarers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The use of wearable health monitoring technologies shows great promise in helping female sailors achieve a better work-life balance. Evaluating how successfully these technologies promote well-being and reduce the mental and physical stresses of marine vocations is the main goal. Our goal is to examine how real-time health monitoring might help reduce stress, improve sleep patterns, and promote a healthy lifestyle in the demanding world of sailing. To help women seafarers keep up their health and thrive despite the specific demands of their job, we’re looking at how wearable tech might improve work-life balance. To better meet the requirements of women in the marine sector, investigating the association between technology adoption and enhanced quality of life is essential. By doing so, it is possible to develop targeted support measures for them. Wearable health monitoring impact data for five different device IDs shows a wide range of values for the following: heart rate (bpm): 67-98, steps (504711666), step hours (4.87-8.17), calories burned (1687-2680), and work-life balance score (1.57-6.61). For five separate device IDs, the corresponding physical activity impact data shows step counts ranging from 5647 to 13456, active minutes from 90 to 180, calories burnt from 1750 to 3000, sleep quality from 6.5 to 9.1, and work-life balance scores from 3.2 to 7.9.

articleTitle: EnsemBEP: A Robust Ensemble Model for Enhanced B-cell Epitope Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: B-cell epitope prediction has found its use in understanding B-cell recognition spots on a number of antigens that is vital in vaccine design and immunotherapy. These fields urgently need powerful prediction models, but the existing methods often fail to satisfy the requirement of both high sensitivity and high specificity. In response, this manuscript presents an ensemble model named EnsemBEP that combines Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost for improving the performance of B-cell epitope prediction. New model for epitope prediction, named EnsemBEP shows better performance in comparison with other models including EpiDope and BepiPred-2.0. The proposed EnsembEP model demonstrates superior performance compared to existing models such as EpiDope and BepiPred-2.0. Through rigorous evaluation, EnsemBEP achieved an AUC of 0.945, accuracy of 0.885, sensitivity of 0.823, specificity of 0.926, and an MCC of 0.743. All these findings point out that EnsemBEP yield better results than competing models thereby confirming that it is more accurate and reliable in predicting B-cell epitopes. The results provide evidence for the significance of ensemble learning methodologies in attaining higher predictive performance in immunoinformatic.

articleTitle: A Review of Resource Allocation of OFDMA using LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: To address the challenge of distributed resources in multi-carrier communications, various approaches have been proposed. These methods typically stem from information-theoretic measurements or other channel activity aspects, which may not accurately represent the coding. This study employs a customized optimization method for Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), implemented with a Low-Density Parity Check (LDPC) codes and employing general stability conditions. The latter involves formulating a crucial requirement to ensure flawless decoding by the Belief Propagation (BP) decoder with no errors in the received vector. This reframes the overall condition to represent better the characteristics of useful multi-carrier systems such as OFDM and establishes a broad framework for resource allocation to maximize transmitted power based on the attributes of LDPC coding. This study describes that the suggested optimization method that is applied in Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiple Access (OFDMA) systems for power distribution to ensure reliable decoding while minimizing power consumption. To validate the proposed approach, it is compared with information-theoretic methods aiming to maximize the mutual information shared by the transmitter and receiver. Both approaches yield practically the same performance for the scenarios addressed in this study.

articleTitle: Optimizing Predictive Maintenance in Smart Factories Using Random Forests and Internet of Things Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of Industry 4.0, smart factories leverage advanced technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning to enhance operational efficiency. Predictive maintenance (PdM) is a critical aspect of this transformation, aiming to anticipate and mitigate equipment failures before they occur. However, existing PdM models often suffer from high false positive rates and inadequate scalability. This study addresses these issues by proposing an optimized predictive maintenance framework utilizing Random Forests and IoT sensors, tailored specifically for smart factory environments. Our methodology integrates a comprehensive IoT sensor network within the factory, collecting real-time data on various parameters such as temperature, vibration, and machine utilization. This data is preprocessed to handle noise and outliers, followed by feature extraction to identify the most significant predictors of equipment failure. We employ an optimized Random Forest algorithm, enhanced with a novel dynamic threshold adjustment technique and an adaptive learning mechanism to improve prediction accuracy and model robustness. The model’s performance is evaluated using a large dataset collected from multiple manufacturing units over a period of six months. The proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional PdM approaches. Our optimized Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6. 8 \%}$, a precision of $\mathbf{9 4. 5 \%}$, and a recall of $\mathbf{9 7. 2 \%}$, compared to ${88.3 \%, 85.7 \%}$, and 89.1% respectively for the baseline models. Additionally, the dynamic threshold adjustment technique reduced the false positive rate by 40%, while the adaptive learning mechanism enhanced the model’s ability to generalize.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Classification with Federated Learning through a Flower Simulation Study on the CIFAR100 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The aim of this study is to enhance image classification using Federated Learning (FL) applied to the CIFAR100 dataset. We created a decentralized FL environment with multiple clients, leveraging the Flower framework and Ray for distributed computing. The methodology involved federated averaging for parameter updates, client-specific data handling, and performance evaluation using various metrics. Our results demonstrate a significant improvement in model performance, with loss decreasing from 0.060846 to 0.038253 and accuracy increasing from 41.64% to 57.96% over five training rounds. This study concludes that FL is effective in improving image classification while preserving data privacy and decentralization.

articleTitle: Design of a Drug Smart Traceability System in the Pharmaceutical Supply Chain using Dynamic Non-Fungible Tokens
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Current Drug Supply Chain (DSC) includes numerous independent participants with assorted interests. Today, DSC is confronted by several serious challenges related to shipping, special storage, traceability, and expiration, as well as ensuring sustainable access and availability of essential medicines. Furthermore, the number of counterfeit drugs has increased radically, causing thousands of individuals to be affected by poisoning and medical negligence. To address these issues, this research develops an effective track and trace model, calledLotTrace which leverages the Internet of Things (IoT), Blockchain Technology (BCT) and Non-Interchangeable Tokens (NITs) to trace drug lots from manufacturing process to consumption. NIT is a distinctive digital identifier of physical and virtual assets logged on a BCT to attest to proprietorship and legitimacy. LotTrace uses smart contracts and Hyperledger technology for dependable and effective traceability of pharmaceutical products. The lot details are updated across the chain, and erstwhile information is continuously logged in the ledger blocks. It instigates traceability by allocating inimitable identifiers to drug lots and logs incidents and signposts, providing an end-to-end traceability that allows partakers to authenticatethe genuineness and provenance of the drug products. LotTrace mints virtual tokens to digitize the metadata such as the certifications, present owner, current location, environmental conditions of a drug lot. After gathering these essential data from the drug manufacturer, metadata will be included based on shipping environmental conditions to mint Dynamic NIT (dNIT). This information is recorded in the BitTorrent File System (BTFS) to build a real-world storage infrastructure. Ratified stakeholders can access this information using the smart contracts. This work creates an NIT smart contract on the ERC1155 standard using the Remix Integrated Development Environment (IDE). LotTrace exploits BTFS to solve the issue of processing big documents on the Web 3.0 ecosystem and guarantees that the information are immutably stored in a secured way. This systemrecords the drug attributes and its appropriate metadata during itslife cycle from manufacturing to consumption. The research also provides testing details and evaluates the feasibility of tracing solution. This study evaluate the effectiveness of LotTrace system in terms of the cost of system transactions.

articleTitle: Classification of Brain Tumor Detection Techniques - A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Tumors present in brain remains a significant global health issue, affecting millions annually and presenting various diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. These tumors originate from irregular cell growth in the brain and its surrounding tissues, and their treatment varies based on the location, and severity of the tumor. Timely and precise diagnosis is essential for enhancing patient outcomes, but it remains challenging due to the variability and complexity of brain tumors. The complexities involved in identifying and treating different types of tumors highlight the need for advanced diagnostic tools. Recent developments in brain tumor detection highlight important technological innovations, particularly the use of artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning (DL), and advancements in imaging techniques. In particular, we examine the role of machine learning algorithms, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and You-Only-Look-Once (YOLO), which have enhanced the precision, speed, and accuracy of tumor detection. Furthermore, emerging trends in non-invasive imaging methods and their potential to transform early diagnosis and personalized treatment strategies are explored.

articleTitle: Approaches to Mapping and Zonation of Groundwater Potential Mapping through Multi-Agent Optimization in GIS
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The groundwater resources utilization has encountered significant difficulties as a result of the depletion of surface-water supplies and recurrent droughts. Moreover, groundwater potential status detailed analyses have been necessary for the best handling of such valuable resources. In order to determine the water shortage and analyse the water index for Thiruvallur district, Tamil Nadu, a method integrating Remote Sensing (RS), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and Deep Learning (DL) algorithm (i.e., Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)) was utilised in this work and multistage optimization is used for get accurate result. Initially groundwater control elements, comprising nine topographic variables, two hydrological variables, two geological variables, the kind of forest, the type of soil, and the type of land use, have been mapped using RS and GIS information for this reason. Second, predicated on the provided method and the training information, the groundwater potential has been evaluated and plotted. This study categorizes the groundwater and classify them as either very high, high, moderate, low, or very low. In conclusion, the proposed CNN model is capable of assessing the water index and detecting instances of water scarcity. The presented model was evaluated using the following metrics: accuracy, precision, precision, ROC, MAE, MCC, and classification error rate (CEP). The effectiveness of the described method was evaluated by comparing it to current methodologies. The proposed methods have ROC values of 98.76, an accuracy of 99.01%, a precision of 98.87%, and a f1-score of 98.16%.

articleTitle: Hydroponic using Deep Water Culture for Lettuce Farming using Random Forest Compared with Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: This research aims to optimize lettuce cultivation in a Deep Water Culture (DWC) hydroponic system by leveraging machine learning techniques. By analyzing various parameters such as temperature, pH, and nutrient concentration, the study seeks to identify optimal conditions for maximizing lettuce growth and yield. A Random Forest algorithm is employed to predict optimal parameter settings and compare its performance with a Decision Tree algorithm. The Random Forest’s ensemble approach is expected to enhance prediction accuracy and robustness. By optimizing hydroponic parameters through machine learning, this research contributes to sustainable and efficient agriculture, reducing resource consumption and maximizing crop yield.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Predict Cardiovascular Disease with Extra Trees Classifiers and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Research indicates a progressive rise in mortality rates associated with Cardio-vascular disease. The primary causes of heart diseases and reduced blood flow through vessels stem from stress and unhealthy lifestyles. The World Health Organization suggests that current mortality rates are elevated due to widespread gadget addiction and persistent stress in daily life. Machine learning-based prediction systems have been proposed for cardiovascular diseases, leveraging their ability to uncover hidden features and complex relationships. However, these systems often lack precision in identifying the exact cause of the observed outcomes. Specifically, the study aims to enhance the predictive accuracy and robustness of the Extra Trees Classifier by employing novel data preprocessing techniques. Preprocessing helps in removing irrelevant and noisy data, thereby improving the signal-to-noise ratio and enhancing the classifier’s performance. By preprocessing the data, it becomes feasible to extract and select relevant features, facilitating better discrimination between classes and boosting the classifier’s predictive power. To improve features clarity the Novel Extra Trees Classifier (NETC) techniques perform advanced feature selection and data transformation approaches exploring the invisibility, aiming to further improve its predictive accuracy of $\mathbf{9 2. 7 \%}$ and generalization capabilities. When combined with other techniques, evaluate PSO optimization’s effectiveness in enhancing cardiovascular disease prediction models, including accuracy and ROC curve analysis.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Product Quality Evaluation using Hybrid LSTM-FCNN Model and GWO Algorithm for Social Media Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is still in its developing era, and sometimes, struggles are faced in evaluating user sentiment due to the use of traditional models to analyze the relationship structures in social media interactions. To tackle the issue, we proposed an innovative approach Hybrid LSTM neural network and a fully connected neural network (FCNN) integrated with the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm. The objective of this proposed method is to improve sentiment analysis by employing the LSTM to capture the sequence of data and improve the ability of FCNNs to improve feature extraction and the analysis process. The proposed system process initiated with the data preprocessing of input Twitter sentiment dataset transformed into a suitable input to the Hybrid LSTM-FCNN neural network. Then, temporal dependency of the data captured by LSTM and FCNN is used to extract the features. The GWO method mimics the grey wolf hunting behaviour, for optimizing the proposed Hybrid LSTM-FCNN model’s parameters to enhance the classification accuracy. The system models start with the initialization of the model, parameters, and training the models using the dataset to reduce the cross-entropy loss, estimating the testing dataset from unseen data and fine-tuning using GWO as necessary. Results demonstrate significant improvements in sentiment categorization compared to traditional methods. The Hybrid LSTM-FCNN model, enhanced with GWO, effectively captures nuanced sentiment patterns, leading to more accurate classification. Additionally, GWO’s computational efficiency contributes to scalability. In conclusion, our proposed approach offers a promising solution for enhancing product quality evaluation through advanced neural network architectures and optimization algorithms applied to social media sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Empowered Natural Language Understanding Voicebot’s for farmers: Kissan Samvaad Initiative
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The ‘Kissan Samvaad’ work focuses on implementing a closed-domain Chatbot using the RASA Open Source Framework to address the lack of timely access to expert agricultural advice for farmers. Despite the rapid growth of Deep Learning and NLU based Chatbots in various fields, farmers often rely on peer knowledge to solve agricultural problems. Kissan Samvaad aims to bridge this gap by allowing farmers to interact with the Chatbot to specify farmers need. By identifying intents and entities in user inputs, the Chatbot retrieves relevant information from its database to provide remedies and solutions using BERT. Initial testing of Kissan Samvaad has shown promising results, indicating its potential to serve as a valuable resource for farmers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Chili Disease Detection: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach with YOLOv5 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: To minimize crop losses and maintain sustainable agricultural practices, identifying chili disease is imperative. Using the YOLOv5 algorithm, this work suggests a unique hybrid deep learning method to improve the identification of chili diseases. The methodology integrates advanced image preprocessing techniques with the YOLOv5 framework to achieve high accuracy in identifying various chili plant diseases. The proposed system influence a comprehensive dataset comprising labelled images of healthy and diseased chili plants, ensuring robust training and validation. Two significant developments are the use of transfer learning to maximize model performance and the integration of data augmentation procedures to overcome class imbalance. The experimental findings show that our hybrid technique achieves outstanding accuracy, recall, and F1-score metrics, greatly outperforming conventional approaches. The results show that the suggested approach can be a useful tool for early disease diagnosis, allowing prompt treatment and encouraging improved crop management techniques. This research highlights the potential of deep learning in revolutionizing agricultural disease diagnostics, offering a scalable and efficient solution for farmers and agricultural stakeholders.

articleTitle: Detailed analysis of various techniques used for fault detection and analysis in multilevel inverters based on renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: With the advent of industrialization, power generation based on renewable energy sources is so prominent. This in turn leads to a drastic increase in the use of multilevel inverters to drive such high power and high voltage applications. This paper aims at discussing various fault classification techniques used to detect faults. Comparison starts from traditional techniques like fast fourier transform, wavelet transform focuses on fault classification in cascaded ${H}$ bridge nine-level inverter. Comparative fault analysis and classification are presented. Fast Fourier transform and wavelet-based fault classification are few traditional methods used to classify faults in multi-level inverters. With the advent of soft computing techniques fuzzy logic controller based fault classification and mitigation came into practice. Furthermore, machine learning based fault classification based on Support vector machine and various other techniques also contributes to fault diagnosis of multilevel inverters.ANN based fault diagnosis and detection has embarked a trend in this field. Fault classification and detection based on neural networks are widely used in research nowadays. This research study will not only focus to discuss on advantages, disadvantages and application but also will give an insight of various fault possibilities and mitigation techniques available to rectify them. A brief of various renewable energy sources used for every mitigation technique discussed, is also listed to give a clear insight of effective utilization under such energy demand and crisis existing worldwide.

articleTitle: Brain Image Analysis for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection using Ensemble Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The brain disorder known as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) impacts millions of people globally. Accurate and early detection of this condition is of the utmost importance for improving patient outcomes through prompt medical management. Here, we propose a novel approach to searching magnetic resonance images of the brain for signs of Alzheimer’s disease. The primary objective of this research is to develop a trustworthy method for early Alzheimer’s disease detection using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain. Faster intervention and better patient care are made possible by the proposed methodology’s use of machine learning algorithms to increase diagnosis accuracy. The dataset, which was donated by Kaggle, consisted of 2179 brain MR images, providing a comprehensive and diverse set for study. To forecast the onset of Alzheimer’s disease, an ensemble machine learning approach is employed, combining many classifiers like decision tree, linear support vector machine, k-NN, and Gaussian support vector machine. In the end, the ensemble that best fits the brain MR pictures is decided by a simple majority vote. With a precision of $\mathbf{9 9. 3 \%}$, the results of this study show tremendous potential for enhancing the diagnosis and treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. Better outcomes for patients and healthcare efficiency are contributed to by the elapsed time of 0.257534 seconds.

articleTitle: Identity-based Security Enhancement in Cloud Computing: Deep Learning-Powered Threat Detection Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Cloud computing has improved data management but also increased security vulnerabilities, notably identity-based threats including identity spoofing, data breaches, and illegal access. In dynamic cloud systems, typical security methods cannot handle these evolving concerns, highlighting need for complex security measures. Deep learning-powered threat detection was established to improve cloud computing identity-based security. It uses LSTM and CNNs to analyze massive volumes of user behavior data and identify dangers. After training on dataset of many cloud simulation log entries, the framework combats many attack approaches. With false positive rate of less than 1% and 99% accuracy in recognizing identity-based threats, it beat standard machine learning models by 6% and dramatically reduced false warnings. This reduction is necessary to reduce security monitoring teams operating load. The framework processed data in 0.02 seconds per log entry to detect risks in real time. Overall, this deep learning-driven system improves identity-based threat detection in cloud security. Businesses looking to enhance the cloud security can benefit from its false positive rate and accuracy. The framework outperformed older techniques in accuracy by about 6%, proving its superiority in threat identification-based management. Future research could focus on refining model’s efficiency and expanding its relevance to more cloud-based environments.

articleTitle: CNN and Logistic Regression Synergy: Advanced Methods for Casting Defect Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The abstract specifically spotlights the performance of a casting defect result by a modeling Classification. It shows that the model has achieved a very good result for all defect categories, from Blowholes to Swell and Pinhole. It gives: 98.31% for Blowholes, 98.27% for Swell, and also a couple of Pinholes so overall F1-Scores will be again finally evaluated on the Class level as follows: Those metrics show the model very well at finding where these defects are and categorizing them correctly, it is consistent which means reliable. The model is very effective in terms of support and accuracy. It was able to process 3,550 samples for Blowholes, reached an accuracy rate of 99%, as well as dealing with others such as Swells (3460) and Pinholes (35100), getting another wearing a percentage similar level. This observation proves that the model can classify a high percentage of defects correctly, corresponding to a good recall rate, and is consistent across different categories of defectivities which means it also has precision. In summary, the defect detection and classification model is well able to accomplish casting quality control as indicated by its performance metrics. Due to its very high levels of precision, recall, and accuracy, the system generates stable results which are indispensable for measuring quality standards in production plants as well as reducing defect rates.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection System for Robot Operating System using Hybrid Deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Robot operating system (RobotOS) has become an important standard middleware in industry and non-industrial sectors in modern world. Attacks to the RobotOS and its networks are increasing rapidly in recent days. These attacks lead to high risks and significant threats to the robot and its environment. This is because these robot systems are not designed by considering cyber security. Security issues of robot system receive increased attention by malicious attackers. This work presents robot network intrusion detection system (RobotNIDS) by leveraging the convolutional model and gated recurrent models in deep learning. The features of the specified deep learning models are flattened and combined. A low dimensional feature representation of the combined features is constructed by applying non-linear transformation with principal component analysis. Subsequently, two-phase classification model is applied on the low-dimensional features of network connection records to analyze the robot network activity in order to detect and classify attacks. The phase 1 employs KNN and random forest (RFort) classifiers and classification of predictions made in phase 1 is done using logistic regression (LRegn) in phase 2. Parameters of classification models are properly adjusted by considering the accuracy in hyperparameter experimental settings. Experiments on ROSIDS23 dataset shows that the proposed Robot-NIDS performs better than the existing intrusion detection and classification methods with an accuracy of $98.2 \%$ in detecting attacks and $98 \%$ accuracy in classification of attacks. The findings reported in this work demonstrates its ability for monitoring and analyzing robot network connection records to accurately detect the abnormal activity and report it to network administrator.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Recycling Vending Machine Using Raspberry Pi for Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: In the modern world, recycling requires efficient strategies for waste management. Due to environmental concerns, recycling, a crucial component of contemporary society, is expected to rise dramatically worldwide. The waste recycling system assists in the separation of recyclable waste and non-recyclable waste, rewards recyclers, and inspires others to recycle. This work aims to create an IoT-enabled vending machine for trash and waste recycling that improves recycling rates, fosters environmental consciousness, and streamlines waste management via real-time data analytics. This garbage management candy machine labels garbage containers with consistent marks. The barcode shows whether the Garbage may be recycled or not. These bags are put on a conveyor belt, where a barcode reader scans them to identify the waste within. Servo motor components push the bags into the appropriate bins at the end of the conveyor. The remainder of the waste can garbage is thrown out, and the user is given money based on the weight of recyclable waste.

articleTitle: An Improved Diagnostic Approach for Classifying Tomato Leaf Diseases using Ensemble Deep Learning based Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Tomato is one of the most common vegetables that has high commercial importance for abundant production to meet the huge demand world-wide. There are several challenges that put impact on the mass production of tomato, and which are required to be resolved timely. One of the major challenges is tomato leaf diseases where different types of diseases are there which need to be identified correctly to protect the plants, otherwise it can cause severe harm to the plants which ultimately effects the production of tomato. To have a solution, several scientists and researchers have been working on this to classify diseases in a very initial stage. Diseases of the plants can be classified from leaf image, but it’s difficult to identify disease manually by observing through eyes. Deep learning techniques are being used to identify different types of disease using the leaf image. Several existing approaches have been discussed in this study where different detection processes have been proposed. But, in most of the cases, several limitations have been observed regarding the performance of those traditional frameworks. In this study, a novel disease detection approach has been proposed to detect multiple types of tomato leaf disease through analyzing the leaf images. Here, after combing the performances of four CNN models (MobileNetv2, ResNet50, VGG19, VGG16), an ensemble deep learning technique has been applied to identify different types of the tomato leaf disease as well as to classify the healthy and affected leaf. The performance achieved from the proposed ensemble framework ensures optimum accuracy of 96.7% with efficiency. A proper comparative analysis has been presented that supports the novelty and potentiality of the work.

articleTitle: Enhanced Early Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder using Deep Learning and Advanced Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: A neurological condition affecting individuals throughout their lives, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) profoundly impacts behavior, activities, cognition, and socio-communication abilities. Timely detection in children between ages two and three is crucial for early intervention. This study employs standard machine learning techniques, and deep learning techniques to predict ASD. Models are rigorously validated using accuracy, precision, and recall measurements. To provide a centralized framework for researchers, comparative analyses consider application types, simulation techniques, comparison approaches, and input data. Additionally, the study includes the best model prediction, highlighting the model that performed most accurately in predicting ASD. Hyperparameter calculation is integral to the study, with optimized hyperparameters determined through meticulous tuning, enhancing the models’ predictive capabilities and overall performance. The goal of the entire approach is to offer a solid foundation for early ASD diagnosis and intervention.

articleTitle: Real-time Agrochemical Management Solutions using Cloud Computing and K-Nearest Neighbors Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Optimizing pesticides to ensure crop health and productivity while limiting environmental effect is one of the many issues faced by modern agriculture. In this research, it provides a cloud-based, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm-based real-time agrochemical management system. The proposed method allows for effective data processing and analysis by using the computing power of cloud platforms. Environmental factors, crop type, soil properties, and historical data are used to inform the KNN algorithm’s prediction of appropriate pesticide application rates. To provide the most current insights and suggestions, the system incorporates real-time data from a variety of sources, including sensors, satellites, and weather predictions. Enhanced crop yields, decreased costs, and less environmental impact may result from farmers making informed decisions about the use of agrochemicals via continuous monitoring and analysis. The system can be easily deployed and adjusted to many agricultural contexts because of the scalability and flexibility of cloud computing. This method provides a viable strategy for improving pesticide management practices, which in turn promotes sustainable farming and increases food safety.

articleTitle: ML-assisted Defect Detection in Power line Insulators for Reducing Energy Wastage
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Power line insulator defects pose significant risks to the reliability and safety of electrical distribution systems. To provide continuous power supply and preventive maintenance, these problems must be promptly detected. It is common practice to employ an airborne platform-based insulator inspection technique to find the issues. Detecting insulator defects in aerial photographs against complicated backdrops is intriguing yet difficult. This work proposes a novel method for automating the detection of Power line insulator flows using the You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5) object identification algorithm. The proposed method includes Transfer learning, data preparation approaches, and augmentation tactics, which shows the promising potential to improve the insulator fault detection model’s accuracy and recall rates. The proposed method also uses post-processing methods to improve problem localization further and eliminate false positives. We assess the effectiveness of the suggested approach using a real-world dataset made up of pictures gathered from several electricity distribution networks. The outcomes of the experiments demonstrate the potential of the proposed method to precisely and recall rates detect insulator faults.

articleTitle: Quality Prediction of Fruits using Artificial Neural Network and its Application in Food Science
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The nutritional value of fruit has a significant impact on customer satisfaction. Fruit quality and costeffectiveness would enhance customer fulfillment and revenue, according to retailers. The whole supply chain requires rapid and simple techniques for assessing quality. The strawberry is a popular fruit that is valued for its distinctive taste as well as numerous health benefits, including antioxidants and helpful amino acids, which significantly improve the item’s total quality. Therefore, dividing strawberries into desired and undesired groups would help customers and startups decide if the strawberries they buy and sell are desired depending on important factors like color and form. To overcome that, Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) were used in the present research. When Multi-Linear Regression (MLR) was used, unacceptable prediction results were achieved for every variable. In contrast, it was discovered that the interior functionality attributes may be properly anticipated by applying ANNs. This was particularly true for the overall monomeric anthocyanin $(\mathrm{R} 2=0.943)$ and antioxidant potential. The current research demonstrated that utilizing color positions with ANNs may effectively assess strawberry quality.

articleTitle: Predicting Groundwater Quality with Advanced Deep Learning Models: Improving Environmental Management by Addressing Pollution Issues and Obtaining More Accurate Forecasts
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: To ensure clean water for consumption in the future, it is imperative to understand the pollutants and the quality of the existing groundwater. Controlling water pollution and enhancing water management both depend on the ability to predict the water’s purity with high accuracy. Previous studies have shown that when it comes to deep learning models, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) performs better in terms of accuracy and precision than random forest (RF). This study explores the field of water quality assessment by creating a novel method that combines state-of-the-art deep learning algorithms such as artificial neural networks (ANN), long short-term memory (LSTM), bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), gated recurrent units (GRU), convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), and backpropagation neural networks (BPNN). Utilising deep learning techniques to enhance the index’s prediction capacity and accuracy, as well as computing WQI utilising comprehensive water quality metrics, are our main research objectives. Through the use of deep learning models in conjunction with WQI, we hope to uncover patterns and connections in information on water quality that are not visible through conventional means. Plans for groundwater development will benefit from the study’s findings, which will also enhance DL applications for better groundwater quality.

articleTitle: Enhancing Potato Plant Disease Detection using CNNs with Transfer Learning: A Robust AI-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: A crop of global importance, potatoes are particularly vulnerable to illnesses that can result in large losses for farmers. Conventional detection techniques, which depend on manual inspection, are frequently time-consuming and prone to human mistake. In order to overcome this, Transfer Learning was combined with Convolutional NeuralNetworks (CNNs) to create an improved disease detection method, utilizing pre-trained models like ResNet50 and VGG16. A collection of more than $\mathbf{3 0, 0 0 0}$ high-resolution images of potato leaves, categorized into healthy and diseased classes, was used to evaluate the effectiveness of this technique. Through model optimization and data augmentation, the methodology yielded an accuracy of about $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$, much surpassing that of conventional models such as Random Forest and Support Vector Machines, which yielded approximately 88% and 85% accuracy, respectively. Furthermore, the model’s effectiveness and scalability were demonstrated by the application of Transfer Learning, which cut training time by almost 40%. This invention provided a reliable approach for early and accurate disease management in potato cultivation, improving accuracy over traditional methods by 11%. ResNet50: Residual Network 50 layers, VGG16: Visual Geometry Group 16 layers

articleTitle: Automated System for Saree Putta Cutting and Rolling using Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The Putta Cutting Machine is an innovative solution designed to automate the precise and efficient cutting of fabric putta (ornamental design of a saree or other traditional garments). Traditional methods of putta cutting are time-consuming and labour-intensive, often resulting in inconsistencies in cut quality and design. This machine aims to overcome these challenges by offering a mechanized approach that ensures uniformity, accuracy, and speed. Equipped with advanced sensors and programmable cutting mechanisms, the Putta Cutting Machine allows for custom designs and patterns to be replicated with high precision. The system reduces material waste and enhances productivity, making it ideal for large-scale textile manufacturers. Moreover, the machine’s userfriendly interface allows operators to input specific cutting parameters, enabling versatility for various fabric types and designs. By streamlining the putta cutting process, this machine significantly reduces labour costs while ensuring consistency in quality, positioning it as an essential tool in the textile and garment manufacturing industry.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bird Species Classification with PaliGemma and Custom EfficientNet Architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Bird species classification is a critical task in biodiversity studies, ecological research, and conservation efforts. Our research presents a comprehensive approach to bird species classification using a custom-modified EfficientNet-B0 model, enhanced with a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) block to improve feature sensitivity. The dataset used comprises a diverse collection of bird images, which are preprocessed and split into training, validation, and test sets. The custom model incorporates the SE block into the EfficientNet-B0 structure, with a dropout layer and a connected layer added for classification. Using an additional Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) block to improve feature sensitivity and a specifically tailored EfficientNet-B0 model, our work provides a comprehensive approach to bird species classification. The dataset consists ofseveral hundred preprocessed images of birds, split into test, validation, and training sets. For classification, the dropout layer and connected layer are added, and the custom model integrates the SE block into the EfficientNet-B0 framework. In our model design, the learning rate is adjusted as needed using a learning rate scheduler, and SGD is employed for model training. The findings show that the custom EfficientNet-B0 model boosts classification accuracy highlighting how well the SE block works to improve model performance.The paper shows deep learning methods for animal tracking and conservation. Index Terms- Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Squeeze-and-Excitation block, Deep learning, EfficientNet-B0,Fine-grained Image Classification Bird Species Classification neural networks wildlife monitoring pali jewel

articleTitle: Role of Blockchain in Automation of Trending Industrial Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The distributed ledger aspect of blockchain technology has transformed traditional trade; each record in this ledger is secured by cryptographic technique, making it more protected and tamper-proof, and the technology is currently attracting more and more attention. Despite warnings of blockchain’s doom, the technology has made tremendous strides and introduced game-changing innovations to the world of digital currency and transactions. Artificial Intelligence (AI), edge computing, machine learning, robotics, cyber physical systems, Industrial Integration (II), and Service Oriented Computing are some of the emerging technologies that support Industry 4.0. The majority of industrial data management systems are centralized and do not provide the capabilities necessary to guarantee trustworthy data provenance, immutability, transparency, auditability, or traceability. A new and potentially gamechanging technology, blockchain promises to decentralize and secure all data and transactions without the interception of trustworthy authority, all while providing trustworthy traceability, transparency, auditability, and immutability. The groundwork for presenting and showing the role of blockchain technology in various scenario is covered in this article. Moreover, we go into key ideas behind industry 4.0 and how this trending technology may be used to its advantage. We investigate many potential applications of blockchain technology to promote the growth of Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Logistic Regression to Detect Breast Cancer using Cross Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Many women in the world are suffering from cancer. Breast cancer is among one of the cancer which is affecting women all over the globe. The machine learning algorithms are found good for detecting breast cancers. Logistic Regression is among the best supervised machine learning algorithms which is found very good in detecting breast cancer. Many hospitals provided their data of females which comes for breast cancer detection. WDBC is one of the best known data sets for breast cancer. K-fold cross-validation reduces the possibility of overfitting and enhances generalization by repeating the process across all folds and computing the average performance. By applying the Logistic Regression model with cross validation we can more effectively generalize to new data. Through the identification of the most significant predictors, feature selection further enhances the model by lowering computational complexity and dimensionality. The findings show that good accuracy for breast cancer prediction is obtained when using Logistic Regression in conjunction with cross-validation. The model is a good fit for clinical applications because of its robust performance, ease of interpretation, and simplicity. The findings of this study demonstrate the validity of logistic regression as a tool for the diagnosis of breast cancer and imply that its combination with cross validation improves diagnostic accuracy and aid in clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Design of a Hybrid AI- based Phishing Website Detection using LSTM, CNN, and Random Forest based Ensemble Learning Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Phishing attacks are always surfacing as key threats against internet users, necessitating advanced detection methods. Blacklist-based systems and rule-based models of phishing detection generally have had critical limitations in dealing with evolving tactics and new phishing schemes. Some of these approaches fail to cope with the temporal and visual patterns of phishing sites, which are crucial for timely and accurate detection. To overcome these difficulties, this work introduces a hybrid AI-based phishing website detection model that utilizes several machine learning and deep learning techniques to improve the accuracy of the detection and remove false positives. The proposed model uses LSTM networks, Genetic Algorithms, Random Forest, and CNN through the stacking ensemble framework. Since LSTM is adopted to capture the temporal dependencies in the website traffic and user interaction patterns, this model can effectively model their phishing behavior over time. GA is used for bioinspired feature selection to reduce the dimensionality of features while optimizing model performance. Random Forest is used as a base layer addressing structured features like URL characteristics and WHOIS information. CNNs are incorporated to extract feature content from a webpage and images that carry various visual indicators often used in phishing attacks including counterfeit logos or banners. A meta-classifier is then used to combine the outputs of LSTMs, CNN, and RF and generate the final classification to boost the detection rate. The proposed hybrid model surpasses the existing techniques and facilitates the analysis of temporal, visual, and structured data, making the detection considerably more accurate. Achieving accuracy of as much as 96-97% and having an AUC of 0.97 with a false positive rate below 3%, the model then impacts the more powerful and more flexible phishing detection system, which is then capable of being more protective against higher sophisticated phishing techniques with increased precision and fewer false alarms.

articleTitle: Sustainable Aquaculture Management through IoT and Deep Learning-Driven Remote Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Aquaculture, as a critical component of global food security, faces challenges in maintaining optimal conditions for aquatic organisms. The paper presents an innovative IoT and Deep Learning-based remote monitoring system designed to enhance sustainable aquaculture management. In order to monitor water quality factors including temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and feeding behavior in real time, the system incorporates a network of sensors. These sensors’ data are locally processed on edge devices before being sent to a cloud-based platform for centralized storage and analysis. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), in particular, are used in deep learning algorithms for image identification tasks to track the health and activity of fish. The system utilizes YOLOv8 for real-time detection and classification of fish diseases, ensuring early intervention and minimizing losses. User-friendly interfaces provide actionable insights through smart dashboards displaying trends, alerts, and recommended actions based on predictive analytics. By facilitating proactive management decisions, this IoT and Deep Learning-based system aims to optimize resource utilization, improve productivity, and promote sustainable practices in aquaculture. Case studies demonstrate its efficacy in enhancing operational efficiency, reducing environmental impact, and fostering long-term viability in aquatic food production systems.

articleTitle: Early Landslide Detection Using Multi-Sensor Data and IoT-Based Alert Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The “Early Landslide Detection System” utilizes IoT to monitor and detect landslide risks in real-time. An artificial rain setup simulates rainfall on a model mountain, with a rain sensor, soil moisture sensors, and vibration sensors tracking rainfall, soil saturation, and ground movement. Data is logged on ThingSpeak, and once significant vibrations are detected, the system alerts users through the Blynk app via mobile notifications and emails. This system provides an efficient, cost-effective solution for early landslide detection, enhancing disaster preparedness and minimizing potential damage.

articleTitle: Analyzing and Classification of Heart Disease using VGG19
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: This study presents a novel method for heart disease classification by integrating the VGG 19 architecture with a 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This approach aims to improve diagnostic accuracy and reduce misdiagnosis risks. It involves preprocessing heart images, selecting relevant features, and applying classification algorithms. The method achieved a $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ accuracy rate in data validation. It uses CNNs for detailed data analysis and comparison, and introduces a hybrid technique combining VGG 19 with a 2D CNN. Various classification models were tested, with the GLCM combined with GoogleNet emerging as the most effective for feature selection and accurate heart disease prediction.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Precision Irrigation for Coconut Plantations: Enhancing Growth and Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: In agriculture, precision irrigation plays a pivotal role in optimizing crop growth and resource utilization. In this study, must proposean Internet of Things based irrigation remote monitoring system tailored for enhancing coconut plant growth. The system integrates sensor technology, Internet of Things connectivity, and data analytics to provide real-time monitoring and control of irrigation parameters such as soilmoisture, temperature, and humidity. Leveraging a network of sensors deployed in the coconut plantation, the system collects and analyzes environmental data to optimize irrigation schedules and ensure optimal growing conditions for coconut plants. Through a user-friendly interface accessible via web or mobile applications, farmers can remotely monitor the status of their plantation and adjust irrigation settings as needed.Additionally, the system incorporates predictive analytics capabilities to anticipate irrigation needs based on historical data and weather forecasts, thereby enhancing water efficiency and crop productivity. Field trials demonstrate the effectiveness of this Internet of Things based irrigation system in improving coconut plant growth while reducing water consumption and operational costs. This findings underscore the potential of Internet of Things technologies in revolutionizing agricultural practices, facilitating sustainable crop management, and enhancing food security in coconut-producing regions.

articleTitle: Smart Body Protection for Soldiers at Higher Altitudes
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The necessity of monitoring the health of soldiers deployed at higher altitudes has become significant as their life’s became vulnerable mainly due to extreme cold weather conditions. Presented work provides a glimpse of an attempt that was made to monitor the health of a military personnel as a real time data. Extreme cold conditions impact the health of a personnel, hypobaric hypoxia is a condition that is mainly faced by the military personnel deployed at higher altitudes as reduces the physical work capacity of a personnel and in a situation that may lead to death. To reduce the impact in these variety of situations the model is proposed.

articleTitle: Datasets for Aquaculture: A Deep Learning Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Aquaculture is being used to a greater extent for conservation goals, such as species recovery, habitat restoration, and mitigating the effects of wild capture on harvested species that are vulnerable. Deep Learning (DL) models are in use for training datasets of aquatic organisms, to provide solutions to various problems in aquaculture farming. However, there is still motivation, awareness, and knowledge that are found necessary to encourage researchers to explore the potential unmet. In this work, the various aquaculture-associated datasets used in DL for image processing procedures have been elucidated. It addresses the challenges of these datasets to pinpoint areas for improvement, ultimately paving the way for future advancements in the application of DL within aquaculture.

articleTitle: An Improved Churn Prediction Model using Relevance Feature Identification and Personalized Modeling Technique with Optimized Retention Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Churn prediction is vital in customer retention strategies, helping businesses proactively address customer dissatisfaction. In this research, we propose a comprehensive churn prediction model that addresses these challenges by integrating advanced techniques, including handling imbalanced data, feature relevance identification, new feature generation, incorporating temporal patterns, and personalized modeling for customer segments. By applying advanced techniques such as SMOTE-ENN for balancing, RFE-RF for feature elimination, and K-Means clustering for segmentation, the model improves predictive accuracy and provides actionable insights for targeted retention strategies. The proposed model effectively enhances prediction accuracy and provides actionable insights for customer groups, optimizing retention strategies. With the proposed Model Logistic Regression performs better across all segments in terms of AUC-ROC and precision particularly for high-value and frequent users with $0.91 \%$ and $0.80 \%$ respectively.

articleTitle: Scaling Approach Over Learning Layer of Deep Learning Model to Reduce the FALSE Error in Binary Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Objective: Worldwide Breast cancer is a main health issue for the women, every year thousands of deaths occurring due to late detection and diagnosis. Computer-aided diagnostic detection systems are becoming a useful tool for early cancer cell identification. The proposed work uses the Deep Learning, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), model to identify the cancerous cells in medical imaging accurately. Method: The proposed work balances the Learning Layers (LL) of CNN model to find the finest binary classification to detect whether the given image is Malignant or Benign. Experiment is carried out on gradual scaling of LL from 1 to 5 with learning cycles 10,15 and 20 respectively for each stage of scale to reduce the False Positive (FP), False Negative(FN) errors in each layer. Result: The performance of the scaled LL is evaluated using the metric like residual error loss, training accuracy in training stage. The model is evaluated with precision, recall, accuracy and $\mathbf{f 1}$-score in the testing stage. By leveraging the power of deep learning, the system achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 97% in differentiating between the two common types of cancer cells in CNN-LL5.

articleTitle: Walk Well: Smart Sensor based Wearable Leg Support Exoskeleton with Fall Alert
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: Falls are a major public health concern that requires creative ways to lessen their effects, especially for older folks and those in vocational settings. Having seen the potentially disastrous effects of falls, we have created a novel method that wears sensors into an exoskeleton and prevents slip-related mishaps before they happen. Our technology combines small inertial measurement devices positioned strategically on the lower limb with an advanced combination of wearable sensors, including heart rate and pulse oximetry monitoring. All of these sensors work together to create a strong network that can identify slips immediately. This exoskeleton is essential in helping people do gait recovery techniques since it is precisely controlled in terms of torque. Through its ability to react quickly to detected slips, the exoskeleton can potentially avoid loss of balance and stop a series of event that could result in more catastrophic injuries, like hip injuries. Our technology operates in real-time, it guarantees prompt and flexible reactions, providing a proactive defense against slips and falls, which are frequently unpredictable.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model using Tsetlin Machine to Predict HbA1c Levels in Homeopathy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The application of the Tsetlin Machine to predict HbA1c levels in diabetes patients treated with homeopathy focuses on improving accuracy in personalized diabetes management. The primary aim is to use the Tsetlin Machine’s pattern recognition capabilities to identify key factors, such as treatment duration, blood glucose trends, insulin sensitivity, lifestyle factors, and comorbid conditions, that influence HbA1c levels. This approach offers a reliable, non-invasive model to assist clinicians in optimizing homeopathic treatments for better glycemic control. By analyzing historical patient data, the machine detects correlations between treatments and HbA1c outcomes, allowing for more effective diabetes management. Data from two instances in the HbA1c_Prediction_Dataset was taken as a sample. In the first instance, five features were analyzed for five patients, with blood glucose trends ranging from 0.2196 to 0.9944 and insulin sensitivity from 0.0021 to 0.7692. The second instance examined fasting blood sugar (0.1995 to 0.7831) and BMI (0.2200 to 0.9511) among other factors. This method supports enhancing predictive accuracy for patients undergoing homeopathic treatment for diabetes.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Deep Learning Process to Predict Textile Industry Fabric Quality Evaluation using Artificial Intelligence Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Electronics, Communication and Aerospace Technology (ICECA)
abstract: The textile industry is highly dependent on maintaining stringent quality standards to ensure product consistency, reduce defects, and meet consumer expectations. This paper presents an intelligent deep learning process for evaluating fabric quality in the textile industry using advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. The proposed hybrid model integrates EfficientNet for feature extraction, GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) for sequential data handling, and XGBoost for robust classification. The model was trained and tested on fabric images, evaluating parameters like fabric density, texture patterns, and defects. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed model achieved the highest accuracy of 93.45%, surpassing traditional models like CNN, LSTM, SVM, and Random Forest. Furthermore, the model also excelled in precision, recall, and F1-score, highlighting its robustness and suitability for real-time fabric quality evaluation in industrial applications. The superior performance of the model underscores the potential of AI-driven approaches in improving textile quality assurance processes.
